cover.headline: One molecule turned a generic-intermediates maker into a 36%-margin business; the market pays ~50x Sep-28E EPS for it, our rule gives 34.5x: target {{dcf.tp|inr}}, SELL
cover.lead: Acutaas Chemicals (formerly Ami Organics) makes advanced intermediates for drug makers (88% of FY26 revenue of ₹1,339 cr) and specialty chemicals (12%). FY26 profit more than doubled to ₹356 cr as a 10-year contract to supply darolutamide intermediates to Orion's Fermion (for Bayer's prostate-cancer drug Nubeqa) scaled to ~₹635 cr, ~47% of revenue, and the EBITDA margin jumped from 23% to 36%. Q1FY27 revenue rose 59%. We forecast EPS of ₹49.6 / 60.4 / 71.7 for FY27-29E, 7-18% below the street for FY27-28, mainly because we do not forecast forex gains or high other income. The brokers that disclose a method use **P/E**, and so do we: Acutaas's median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2022 (31.8x), lifted 7.8% for the pharma sector's move over the same window, gives **34.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹66.1 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL**. Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹2,123; DCF ₹1,170. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.p: Gross margin 45% → 58% and EBITDA margin 23% → 36% in one year; Q4FY26 42%. ROE back to 24% with net cash (₹314 cr at Jun-2026). Strong chemistry: 90%+ backward integration and 50-90% global shares in key intermediates (trazodone, dolutegravir, entacapone).

arguments.h: But it rests on one molecule
arguments.p: CDMO was ~47% of FY26 revenue, mostly darolutamide for one customer, and explains almost all of the margin jump. Nubeqa's patents run to 2033 (US) and 2035 (EU). The base business of generic intermediates was flat in FY24-26 (₹511 → 539 cr).

arguments.h: New engines are early and lower-margin
arguments.p: Battery electrolyte additives started supplying in Q1FY27 (4,000 MT, ~15% target margin, against Chinese incumbents); semiconductor chemicals are ₹16 cr today (BFC) with the Korean plant earning from FY28; a ₹212 cr electronic-chemicals plant comes by end-FY28. They dilute margins before they add much profit.

arguments.h: The price pays for the future, our rule pays for the past
arguments.p: ₹3,279 is 69.5x trailing and 54.3x our FY28E EPS, ~50x Sep-28E. Acutaas's own forward P/E since Apr-2022 has a median of 31.8x because the market did not foresee the FY26 jump; the DCF needs ~28% growth for 15 years. The street median target is ₹3,790; ours is far lower.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): Q2 is seasonally stronger than Q1; watch CDMO momentum and the first battery-additive revenue.
Apixaban generics after the Eliquis patent expiry (Nov-2026 onwards): Acutaas has lined up 25-30 generic customers for its intermediates (PL).
Four validated CDMO molecules start contributing in H2FY27 (₹50-100 cr each at peak, after regulatory approvals).
Battery additives: third product trial runs from Q3FY27, fourth product contract; ECMS incentive (up to ~₹30 cr).
Indichem (Korea) customer qualifications in FY27 for revenue from FY28; announcements on the new R&D centre and land for the next pharma plant.

sections.title: A Surat chemist that makes the building blocks of other companies' drugs; one contract-manufacturing molecule now brings almost half of revenue

blocks.p: Acutaas makes **advanced pharmaceutical intermediates**: the chemical steps just before an active ingredient (API). It sells them to two kinds of buyers. (1) **Generic API makers**: for off-patent drugs such as trazodone (an antidepressant), dolutegravir (HIV), entacapone (Parkinson's), apixaban and rivaroxaban (blood thinners) and pazopanib (kidney cancer), where it claims 50-90% of global supply of key intermediates and develops products early, before patents expire, so that it is written into its customers' regulatory filings. (2) **Innovators, under contract (CDMO)**: above all five intermediates for darolutamide (Bayer's prostate-cancer drug Nubeqa), supplied to Orion's API arm Fermion under a 10-year agreement signed in 2022. It does not make APIs itself ("we do not compete with our customers"). Its **specialty chemicals** vertical makes commodity-like products (parabens, methyl salicylate) at Jhagadia, photoresist chemicals for chip makers at Baba Fine Chemicals, and from Q1FY27 battery electrolyte additives. 1,007 employees; 77% of FY26 product sales were exported.

blocks.callout: **So what:** Acutaas is two companies in one. One is a good but ordinary generic-intermediates maker with strong chemistry, flat revenue in FY24-26 and ~20% margins. The other is a contract supplier to one of the fastest-growing cancer drugs in the world, which turned the group into a 36%-margin business in a year. The specialty-chemicals side is small and is being rebuilt around batteries and semiconductors. Investors are paying for the second company and for the rebuild; most of the risk sits there too.

sections.title: From a Surat lab to a ₹27,000 cr company: an IPO, two acquisitions, a Korean JV, a QIP and a split; two founders have sold 3.3% since

blocks.p: Naresh Patel and Chetan Vaghasia started Ami Organics as a small lab in 1998 and set up the company in 2004 in Sachin, Surat. It grew as a supplier of intermediates for generic drugs, received its first USFDA inspection report in 2018 and listed in Sep-2021. Since then it has bought two plants from Gujarat Organics (Ankleshwar and Jhagadia, FY22-23), 55% of Baba Fine Chemicals (FY24), and set up battery-additive and Korean semiconductor subsidiaries. It renamed itself Acutaas Chemicals in 2025 to signal "a sharper focus on specialty and custom chemical solutions".

sections.title: Industry: CDMO grows ~7% a year, specialty chemicals ~5%, semiconductor chemicals ~12%; Acutaas is a niche player in each

blocks.p: The AR's industry review (citing third-party estimates) puts the global CDMO market at ~USD 166 bn in 2025, growing 7.4% a year to USD 293.6 bn by 2033; India's at USD 8.52 bn, reaching USD 16.53 bn by 2034. Global specialty chemicals are a ~USD 758 bn market growing 4.9% a year; India's ~USD 67 bn. Semiconductor chemicals (USD 16.29 bn in 2025) are forecast to grow 12.1% a year to 2034, and electrolyte additives for lithium-ion batteries ~16% a year to USD 3.4 bn by 2028 (HSIE). Acutaas's FY26 revenue (~USD 155 mn) is a rounding error in all of them. What matters is not market size but the few molecules and products it has chosen: darolutamide, apixaban, a handful of generic intermediates, two battery additives and a few photoresist chemicals.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the tailwinds that drive the next three years (darolutamide, apixaban and other patent expiries) reach Acutaas directly, which is why we forecast ~20%+ revenue growth. The ones the market is most excited about (batteries, semiconductors) are real projects with contracts and plants, but they start small and at lower margins; we include them at modest sizes and do not pay a separate premium for them.

sections.title: CDMO: one contract for one cancer drug took revenue from ₹57 cr to ₹635 cr in two years; the patent clock runs to 2033-35

blocks.p: In CY22 Acutaas signed a 10-year agreement to supply five key intermediates for **darolutamide** to Fermion, the API unit of Finland's Orion; Orion makes the tablets and Bayer sells them worldwide as **Nubeqa**, a prostate-cancer drug approved in ~90 countries. As Nubeqa won new uses (it is being tested across almost all stages of prostate cancer), Acutaas's CDMO revenue went from ₹56.8 cr in FY24 to ₹282.2 cr in FY25 and ~₹635 cr in FY26 (PL, company data), ~47% of group revenue. Bayer raised its peak-sales guidance for Nubeqa from over EUR1bn to over EUR3bn and expected ~50% growth in 2026. Management guides CDMO revenue of ₹1,000 cr by FY28 and says it is "confident to beat" it. Four more CDMO molecules were validated in FY26 (cardiovascular and oncology, per JM) and should start in H2FY27 once their owners get approvals, at ₹50-100 cr each at peak.

blocks.p: Acutaas does not disclose customers above 10% of revenue, and it refuses to split CDMO from the rest ("we are not giving any split", Q1FY27 call). But the arithmetic is clear: if CDMO was ~₹635 cr in FY26 and darolutamide the "majority" of it, one molecule for one customer brought something like 40% of revenue and far more of the profit, since the group margin rose 13 points as CDMO went from 28% to 47% of sales. Kotak Institutional Equities cut the stock to Reduce in Jul-2026 on exactly this point and values the Nubeqa stream separately because of its patent expiry. Management's answer is diversification over time: 30-40 new molecules a year into development, four validated CDMO products and "slowly, slowly, it will derisk our revenue concentration" (Q1FY27 call).

blocks.callout: **Our read:** the darolutamide contract is excellent business while it lasts: patented, growing, filed in the innovator's dossiers and already supplied from built capacity. But it ends in substance when generics arrive (2033 in the US, 2035 in Europe), and a single drug's growth can slow (destocking, a second source, a competing therapy) long before that. We model CDMO at +35% / +18% / +15% in FY27-29E, reaching the ₹1,000 cr guide in FY28; the bear case is built on darolutamide orders flattening.

sections.title: The base business: strong market shares in generic intermediates, but flat revenue in FY24-26 while low-margin products were dropped; apixaban is the next lever

blocks.p: Excluding CDMO, Acutaas's pharma intermediates brought ~₹511 cr in FY24, ~₹572 cr in FY25 and ~₹539 cr in FY26 (company vertical revenue less PL's CDMO series). Management says volumes grew while it "reshuffled" the portfolio in 9MFY26, dropping low-margin products, and that the business grew again from Q4FY26; in Q1FY27 the whole pharma vertical grew 76.5%, with CDMO, "top products" and "a couple of new products" all contributing. The model is to develop an intermediate for an off-patent drug years ahead, get written into generic customers' filings and win a dominant share once the patent expires: 70-90% of key intermediates for trazodone, 70-75% for dolutegravir and ~80% for entacapone (FY21 data). The next big one is **apixaban** (Eliquis, ~USD20 bn of sales), whose exclusivity ends from 2026-28; Acutaas says supplies "have already started picking up" and PL counts 25-30 generic customers lined up. JM estimates a ₹440 cr opportunity if Pfizer keeps 20% of the market after Nov-2026.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** management is right to leave commodity chemicals, and the battery plant is real (built, contracted, supplying). But battery additives are a lower-margin, China-priced product, and semiconductor chemicals have so far shrunk under Acutaas's ownership. We put ~₹400 cr of battery and semiconductor revenue in FY29E, ~16% of the total, at blended margins below the group's. sections.title: Capacity: Sachin is full and Ankleshwar fills by ~FY28, so land, an R&D centre and a ₹212 cr electronics plant come next

blocks.p: Acutaas has ~1,100 KL of reactors across three Gujarat plants, plus the battery block at Jhagadia, BFC's small Greater Noida unit and Indichem in Korea. Utilisation in Q1FY27 was 83% at Sachin ("hitting the capacity utilization roof"), 23% at the rebuilt Ankleshwar plant (expected to fill by ~FY28) and 55% at Jhagadia. So the pharma side has room for about two years; after that it needs a new site, which is why the company is looking for land and plans a new R&D centre with ten times today's capacity. Neither amount has been announced. In Aug-2026 the board approved ₹212 cr for a plant making up to 81,000 MTPA of electronic-grade chemicals in Gujarat, due by end-FY28. The FY23-30 plan already spent or committed ~₹1,000 cr: pharma ~₹320 cr (done), battery ~₹220 cr, Indichem ~₹200 cr, a pilot plant ~₹25 cr and solar ~₹50 cr.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: real in process chemistry and in the darolutamide lock-in; weak in spread; unproven in the new businesses

blocks.p: A moat is a lasting advantage that lets a company earn more than its cost of capital for longer than rivals. Acutaas has two genuine ones and one big weakness. The first is chemistry: it makes hundreds of intermediates up to the step before the API, with 90%+ backward integration, and has won 50-90% shares in several molecules by entering early and doing difficult reactions cheaply. The second is regulatory lock-in on darolutamide: once an intermediate is in an innovator's approved process, switching suppliers takes years. The weakness is spread: one molecule now pays a large part of the bills, and the generic side competes on price with Indian and Chinese rivals. In batteries and semiconductors it has no record yet.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** a narrow moat, real but dated. The chemistry advantage explains why Acutaas earned ~20% margins on generic intermediates for years; the darolutamide lock-in explains the jump to 36%. The first is durable but modest; the second is strong but has an end date (2033-35) and sits with one customer. We would pay for the chemistry and for darolutamide's remaining patent life, not for a moat in batteries or chips that has not been shown.

sections.title: Strongly seasonal: Q1 is always the weakest quarter and Q4 the strongest; H1 is ~40% of the year

blocks.p: Acutaas says the same thing every year: "Q1 is lower than Q2, Q2 is lower than Q3, Q3 is lower than Q4. In last 15 years, it is like that" (CMD, 30-Apr-2026). With ~600 customers and 100+ products ordering at different times, H1 brings ~40% of revenue and H2 ~60%. The pattern held in FY25 (₹177 cr in Q1 to ₹308 cr in Q4) and FY26 (₹207 cr to ₹433 cr), and Q1FY27 fell 24% from Q4FY26 to ₹330 cr while growing 59% YoY. Margins follow revenue because a third of costs are fixed: the EBITDA margin was 24.6% in Q1FY26 and 42.4% in Q4FY26.

sections.title: Revenue ×5.6 in six years; the EBITDA margin doubled to 36% in FY26 when the darolutamide CDMO contract scaled; EPS ₹4.1 to ₹43.5

blocks.p: Acutaas grew revenue from ₹240 cr in FY20 to ₹1,339 cr in FY26, 33.2% a year. For five years the margin barely moved: EBITDA was 17-24% of sales from FY20 to FY25 because most products were generic intermediates sold on price, and the FY22 purchase of two Gujarat Organics plants added low-margin commodity chemicals. FY26 broke the pattern. CDMO revenue (mostly five intermediates for darolutamide, Bayer's prostate-cancer drug Nubeqa, supplied to Orion's API arm Fermion) rose from ₹57 cr in FY24 to ₹282 cr in FY25 and ~₹635 cr in FY26 (PL, company data), while low-margin generic products were dropped. Gross margin went from 45.2% to 57.7%, EBITDA doubled to ₹480 cr (35.9%) and attributable profit rose 124% to ₹356 cr, helped by ₹32 cr of forex gains. FY24 is distorted by a ₹32 cr write-off of a US research joint venture (EPS ₹5.80 reported, ~₹10.1 before it).

blocks.p: In FY21-26 Acutaas generated ₹617 cr of operating cash flow and spent ₹1,041 cr on capex (incl. the Indichem plant), plus ₹68 cr for 55% of BFC. It raised ~₹800 cr of equity (₹300 cr around the IPO, ₹37 cr in FY24, ₹499 cr in FY25) and ended FY26 with ₹198 cr of net cash. Return on capital employed was 32% in FY26 (Screener; the company's version excluding cash and CWIP: 39.3%) and ROE 24.0%, up from 16-21% in FY23-25. Dividends are token: ₹2.50 a share for FY26 (~6% of EPS, 0.1% yield). blocks.p: **Where we stand.** Our EPS is 7-18% below the street and our multiple well below PL's. The P/E gap matters most. Acutaas's own one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2022 has a median of 31.8x; pharma peers re-rated 7.8% above their medians over the same window; 31.8x × 1.078 gives 34.5x. The street pays ~50-56x because it treats FY26's step-change as the new base and extrapolates ~20-25% growth from there; our rule pays the stock's own history, which includes years when the market valued a lower-margin business. Both are honest views; the rule's result is a SELL.

exhibit.title: Critiques we take seriously
head: Argument
rows: Concentration: CDMO (mostly darolutamide intermediates for one customer) was ~47% of FY26 revenue and the source of the margin jump; Kotak Institutional Equities downgraded to Reduce on exactly this (27-Jul-2026).
Patent clock: Nubeqa's key patents run to 2033 in the US and 2035 in Europe (UK 2029); generic darolutamide would end the premium economics of the anchor contract within ~7-9 years.
The base business is not growing: pharma intermediates excluding CDMO were ₹511 cr (FY24), ₹572 cr (FY25) and ₹539 cr (FY26) as low-margin products were dropped.
New engines are early and lower-margin: battery additives target ~15% EBITDA at full use and compete with Chinese suppliers; Indichem starts revenue only in FY28; BFC has shrunk for three years.

sections.title: Valuation: 34.5x Sep-28E EPS gives {{dcf.tp|inr}}; the price pays ~50x and assumes ~28% growth for 15 years

blocks.p: Only two of the seven brokers with notes standing on 30-Sep-2026 disclose a method in what we could read, and both rest on **P/E**: PL values the stock at 56x FY28E EPS, and Kotak Institutional Equities uses a sum of the parts that puts 35x Jun-28E P/E on the business outside the Nubeqa contract and values the Nubeqa stream separately because of its patent expiry. HSIE frames its Sell against the stock's ~41x five-year average one-year-forward P/E. We therefore value on **P/E on Sep-28E EPS (half FY28E, half FY29E)**, with EV/EBITDA and a DCF as cross-checks. Our forecasts carry no exceptional items and minorities are negligible, so reported EPS needs no adjustment.

**Pharma or chemicals?** Screener and NSE classify Acutaas as pharmaceuticals; the company calls itself a specialty-chemicals company and most covering analysts sit on chemicals desks, so the street partly treats it as a specialty chemical. Under PLAYBOOK §7c the nine-name pharma set governs and we keep it in the base (Acutaas is outside the set). We show the chemicals set's move over the same window as a sensitivity: Indian chemical stocks trade −23.3% against their medians since Apr-2022, while pharma trades +7.8%.

Acutaas listed on 14-Sep-2021. Following the batch rule we skip the IPO months and use its one-year-forward P/E **since 1-Apr-2022** on every weekly close plus the 30-Sep-2026 close (236 points): price ÷ the next full fiscal year's EPS. Forward EPS is FY24 for dates in FY23, FY25 for FY24, FY26 for FY25, our FY27E for FY26 and our FY28E for Apr-Sep 2026. FY24 carried a ₹32.1 cr write-off of the US JV (no tax effect), material against ₹43 cr of attributable profit, so the base uses FY24 EPS before it (₹10.1 vs ₹5.80; batch practice A18). The reported-EPS median is the same 31.8x (only the upper percentiles change). Trough rule: reported FY24 EPS (₹5.80) is just above half the prior three-year peak (₹5.7), so no year is left out. We multiply the median by the nine pharma peers' move over the same window (+7.8%) and round to the nearest half-turn. No blend with Acutaas's own move, no growth uplift (sensitivities below).

sections.title: Our honest summary: a real step-change in a good chemistry business, priced as if it were permanent; the rule says SELL

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** a strong process-chemistry company (90%+ backward integration, dominant shares in several generic intermediates) that became a 36%-margin business when its darolutamide contract scaled (~47% of FY26 revenue), with net cash (₹314 cr at Jun-2026), growth of 59% in Q1FY27 and new battery and semiconductor plants starting. **What you are not buying:** diversification (one molecule, one customer), disclosure of that dependence, or a proven record in batteries and chips.

**What you are paying:** ₹3,279 is 69.5x trailing EPS, 54.3x our FY28E and 49.6x Sep-28E. On the street's method (P/E), Acutaas's own 31.8x median since Apr-2022 lifted by the pharma sector's +7.8% gives 34.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹66.1 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): a SELL under the house rule. The EV/EBITDA cross-check (₹2,123) agrees and the DCF (₹1,170) is far lower. Even the most generous rule-based variant (window from the earnings break: 41x, ₹2,710) is below the price; only the street's own multiple (PL's 56x: ₹3,700) justifies it. The street median target (₹3,790) implies little upside too.

CDMO; specialty chemicals incl. battery and semiconductor chemicals) but one segment in its audited accounts; the engine runs one revenue-growth path and the five-line build sits in businessLines, checked against model revenue in tools/authoring/ACUTAAS.ctx.js. EBITDA is on Screener's basis (before other income), which is also the company's basis. assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the five-line build below. FY27 +24.9%: management guides ~25% with Q1FY27 revenue already +59% (CDMO and core intermediates), and H1 is typically ~40% of the year; our FY27 needs Q2-Q4 revenue of ~Rs1,342 cr, +19% on Rs1,132 cr a year earlier. FY28 +22.0% / FY29 +19.7%: CDMO reaches ~Rs1,010 cr in FY28 (guidance Rs1,000 cr, 'confident to beat'), battery additives ramp toward full use of 4,000 MT in three years, Indichem starts in FY28. Street FY27E: PL Rs1,699 cr, HSIE Rs1,722 cr, SBICAP Rs1,770 cr; FY28E Rs2,082-2,323 cr.

base._why: FY26 revenue Rs1,339.4 cr: Advanced Pharmaceutical Intermediates Rs1,174.1 cr + Specialty Chemicals Rs165.2 cr (Q4FY26 deck). CDMO Rs635.1 cr (PL initiation, company data); pharma ex-CDMO Rs539.0 cr by difference; semiconductor (BFC) Rs15.7 cr and commodity chemicals Rs149.5 cr (corporate deck, Mar-2026); battery nil.

businessLines._why: CDMO +35% in FY27 (Bayer expects ~50% Nubeqa growth in 2026; Q1FY27 pharma +76.5%; PL FY27E Rs800 cr), +18% in FY28 (~Rs1,010 cr vs the Rs1,000 cr guide; four validated molecules start in H2FY27, Rs50-100 cr each at peak) and +15% in FY29 as darolutamide growth slows. Pharma ex-CDMO +15/12/10% after a flat FY24-26 (portfolio reshuffle done in 9MFY26; apixaban generics from 2026-28; JM models +12% a year). Battery additives Rs50/160/280 cr: supplies began in Q1FY27, 2,000 MT VC + 2,000 MT FEC fully contracted over three years, a third additive from Q3FY27; PL puts Phase 1 peak revenue at ~Rs380 cr, HSIE FY28 at Rs100-200 cr. Semiconductor Rs25/60/115 cr: BFC recovers from Rs15.7 cr; Indichem revenue from FY28 ('slow start'; HSIE USD20-25 mn within three years of operation). Commodity chemicals -20% in FY27 as they are phased out, then flat-to-up as new products use the same plant. The Rs212 cr electronic-grade chemicals plant (end-FY28) is not in revenue before FY30.

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener/company basis (before other income): 19.9% (FY23), 17.9% (FY24), 23.0% (FY25), 35.9% (FY26; Q4 42.4%), 34.3% in Q1FY27. The jump came from the darolutamide CDMO ramp and dropping low-margin products: gross margin 45% (FY25) to 58% (FY26). Guidance: FY27 margin 'similar' to FY26 ('Q4 is too ambitious'), because lower-margin battery additives offset CDMO growth. Segment build: pharma ~38.5% (Q4FY26 44%, Q1FY27 36%), battery ~5% in FY27 rising to ~15% at full use (PL), semiconductor ~25-30% during Indichem's start-up, commodity ~10-12%. That gives 35.3% / 34.5% / 34.1% for FY27-29; we use 35.5% / 35.0% / 34.5%. Street: PL 35.5/35.4%, HSIE 35.7/36.6/36.4%, SBICAP 35.9/35.6/35.0%.

dcf._betaWhy: Acutaas is net cash, so WACC equals the cost of equity. Beta 1.0 (12.5%): one customer/molecule drives about half of revenue, the chemicals side is cyclical, and the stock has swung widely (Rs434-3,695 since Apr-2022).

dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from 19.7% (FY29E) to 7% by FY42E: revenue grew 33% a year in FY20-26, but much of it is one molecule.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 30% by FY42E, below our FY29E 34.5%: generic darolutamide from the mid-2030s, more battery and commodity-like volume, and price pressure on intermediates.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from 10-15% of sales (FY27-29E) to 7%: maintenance (~3.5% of sales; FY26 depreciation 2.7%) plus growth capex at Acutaas's ~1.5x gross asset turn.
dcf._wcNote: Operating working capital is ~29% of FY26 sales on Screener's Mar-26 balance sheet (other assets less cash, less other liabilities incl. Rs57 cr of minority interest that Screener puts there); the company reports 120 days. The engine holds the ratio, consistent with 99-120 days.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Acutaas: of the brokers that disclose a method, PL uses P/E (56x FY28E) and Kotak Institutional Equities a sum of the parts that puts 35x Jun-28E P/E on the business outside the Nubeqa contract; HSIE frames its SELL against the stock's ~41x five-year average one-year-forward P/E. 34.5x = Acutaas's median one-year-forward P/E since 1-Apr-2022 (listed 14-Sep-2021; IPO months skipped; every weekly close plus the 30-Sep close, 236 points; forward EPS = FY24 before the Rs32.1 cr JV impairment (Rs10.1 vs Rs5.80 reported; the median is 31.8x on reported EPS too), FY25-26 reported, our FY27E/FY28E) of 31.8x x 1.078 (nine pharma peers' trailing P/E at the 30-Sep close vs their medians over the same window, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced +7.8%) = 34.3x, nearest half-turn. Trough rule: FY24 reported EPS Rs5.80 is just above half the prior three-year peak (Rs5.72), so no year is left out. Bull 49x / bear 27x = 75th / 25th percentile (45.4x / 24.9x) x 1.078. No own-move blend, no growth uplift, no chemicals factor (sensitivities only). Written by ACUTAAS.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check: Acutaas's median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since 1-Apr-2022 (EV at each weekly close = price x shares then outstanding less the last published net cash, over the next full year's EBITDA, Screener basis) of 20.1x x 1.075 (the nine peers' EV/EBITDA move over the same window; reproduced +7.5% unrounded) = 21.6x, nearest half-turn, on Sep-28E EBITDA plus Sep-28E net cash. Bull 28.5x / bear 18.5x = 75th / 25th percentile x 1.075.
